question: The printer keeps grabbing several pages at once from the tray, how do I stop that?

answer: When more than one sheet is pulled into the paper path at the same time, fan the stack before loading it
title: Printer User Guide
document:
# Printer User Guide

## Loading the tray

Pull the tray out until it stops and adjust the width and length guides to the paper size. Place the pages print side down with the top edge toward the front of the tray. Do not load pages above the fill line marked inside the tray, and do not mix pages of several sizes or weights in one tray. Push the tray back in until it clicks. The printer detects the paper size from the guides; if the printer reports a size mismatch, check that the guides touch the stack without bending it.

## Stopping a print job

To stop a print job that has already started, press the Cancel button on the printer's control panel. The printer finishes the pages that are already in the paper path and then stops. Several pages may still be printed after the button is pressed, because the printer keeps a few pages in its buffer. To stop a job from the computer, open the print queue and cancel the document there; the printer stops once the queue is empty.

## Paper handling problems

### Multiple sheets feed together

When more than one sheet is pulled into the paper path at the same time, fan the stack before loading it, square its edges, and make sure the sheets are not stuck together by humidity or static. Use paper within the supported weight range and store it flat in its packaging. If the problem continues, the separation pad under the pickup roller is worn and should be replaced.

### Curled output

Paper that curls after printing has usually absorbed moisture. Use a fresh ream, and select the heavier media type in the driver so the fuser runs cooler. Let printed sheets cool flat before stacking them.
